page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.large is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The system provides 2 dedicated physical cores (2 vCPUs) running at 2.8 GHz via the AWS Neoverse-V2 CPU model, configured with one thread per core. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Cache sizing includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is present via AES flags, while standard x86 vector extensions and simultaneous multithreading are absent. The instance includes a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps, carries no bundled local storage, and includes zero GPU accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate solid single-thread performance alongside constrained overall compute capacity due to the two-core allocation. In single-core testing, the instance achieved an average stress-ng score of 1707.19 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1819.0, complemented by a strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 14.33 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics remain within the lower percentiles: multi-core stress-ng registered 3401.99, multi-core Geekbench reached 3239.0, and Clang compilation completed at 4392.0. Uncached read memory bandwidth recorded 56.64 GB/sec in the middle tier, whereas write throughput reached 22.79 GB/sec. Synthetic database metrics logged 3039.26 points in PassMark database operations and 4.57 million operations per second during Redis SET evaluations.

Cost efficiency is realized through the resource balance of ARM-based hardware designed for memory density over extreme parallel compute. By provisioning 16.0 GB of memory across just two physical cores, the instance minimizes compute overhead for applications constrained by working set size rather than thread concurrency. Tradeoffs include modest static web throughput at 5.04 GB/sec, low aggregate PassMark CPU scores, and limited utility for heavy parallelism such as large language model training or extensive ray tracing. The instance is suited for moderate in-memory caches, light database nodes, Redis instances, and standard enterprise applications needing dedicated memory buffers without high thread counts.
